questions.key_step: Take logs of the equal powers to turn each log-ratio into $r/pq$, $p^2/q$, $q^2/pr$.
questions.justification: Several routine stages (three AP gaps, log change of base, exponent equalities, small integer solve) but no real insight; options available. Comparable to a routine chained problem such as 2021-P2-Q1 (L2).

questions.key_step: Inclusion-exclusion with lcm $12$, then remove the $18$ multiples of $48$.
questions.justification: One familiar move (inclusion-exclusion on multiples) followed by plain term counts of A.P.s; options available. Matches 2021-P2-Q17 (inclusion-exclusion, L1).

questions.key_step: Factor and split into partial fractions to telescope.
questions.justification: A single standard trick (telescoping via partial fractions) applied once, with a tidy end evaluation; options available. Easier than 2021-P1-Q15 (telescoping inverse-trig sum, L3).

questions.key_step: G.P. of three logs collapses to $a=c$ (product of the three logs is $1$), then $b=c$.
questions.justification: One small insight (the log-product identity forcing $a=b=c$) followed by a routine A.P. sum; options available. Chain is routine and similar in weight to 2021-P2-Q1 (L2), lighter than 2026-P2-Q6 (L4).

questions.key_step: $a+b=23\lambda+2$ must be odd, so $\lambda$ odd; four sums to count with range bounds.
questions.justification: Routine but multi-step: parity filter, then four boundary-sensitive counts with no insight needed; options help a check. Similar to 2021-P2-Q1 (counting, L2).

questions.key_step: Use $A=\sqrt r+1/\sqrt r$ so that the sum becomes $A^3-2A=21$.
questions.justification: Needs two linked ideas: product gives $a^2r^3=36$, then the reciprocal-symmetric substitution reduces a degree-$9/2$ sum to a cubic in $A$; the cubic must be factored by inspection. Options available. Lighter than 2026-P2-Q6 (L4), above plain routine chains.

questions.key_step: Express $a_1a_4$ as a quadratic in $d$, minimise at the vertex, then $S_n=0$ gives $n=5$.
questions.justification: Routine chain: quadratic minimisation, $S_n=0$ condition and a term evaluation, no real insight. Options available. Comparable to other routine multi-step items such as 2023-P2-Q9 (L2).

questions.key_step: Factor $n^4+n^2+1$ and split into partial fractions to telescope.
questions.justification: One standard trick but the factorisation of $n^4+n^2+1$ must be recognised before telescoping can start, then a careful end-term evaluation. Options available. Easier than 2025-P2-Q15 (numerical telescoping, L4) and 2021-P1-Q15 (L3).

questions.key_step: $S_6-S_5=T_6>1$ and $S_7-S_6=T_7<\frac12$ turn the conditions into $m^2<500<m^3/2$.
questions.justification: Numerical format, no options, with two inequality conditions on partial sums and strict-boundary integer counting; the key reduction ($S_{n+1}-S_n=T_{n+1}$) is simple but the PDF-style route is sign-prone. Nearest in spirit to the GP counting anchor 2021-P2-Q13 (L4), but much lighter.

questions.key_step: General term $k(2k+1)$ of the denominator, then standard power sums and a quadratic in $n$.
questions.justification: Routine chain of standard summation formulas and a quadratic solve; numerical format adds slip risk but no insight is needed. Level 2 like other routine multi-step items (2026-P2-Q3, L2).

questions.key_step: Determinant gives $c-2b=7$, and $c-2b=-A$ because the common difference cancels.
questions.justification: Chain of routine steps: A.P. terms, a simple $3\times3$ determinant, solving for $A$ and $d$, then an A.P. sum; the only observation is that $d$ cancels in $c-2b$. Numerical format, but similar in weight to 2023-P2-Q9 (L2).

questions.key_step: Convert GP and AP conditions to b^2=a/18, 1/a+1/b=20 and eliminate
questions.justification: Two standard progression relations, one substitution and a quadratic with a perfect-square discriminant; no hidden idea, several routine steps. Same weight as 2026-P2-Q12 (L2), which also recovers values from two relations.

questions.key_step: a4*a6 = (ar^4)^2 and a5+a7 = ar^4(1+r^2), divide to get r^2
questions.justification: Routine GP manipulation: two equations, a division, then evaluate a mixed expression. Slightly longer than a one-move item, but nothing non-standard, like 2026-P2-Q3 (L2).

questions.key_step: c2 and c3 give r1+r2 and r1^2+r2^2; r1<r2 assigns ratios; two infinite GP sums
questions.justification: Chain of four routine stages (quadratic for the ratios, ordering, infinite GP sums, evaluate 12a_6+8b_4) with a small precision risk in the ordering; no unfamiliar idea. Comparable to 2026-P2-Q12 (L2).

questions.key_step: Subtract S/2 from S twice to turn b_n into a_{n-1} and a_n into n-1, creating T
questions.justification: The double shift-subtract (arithmetico-geometric style) with boundary terms is a familiar but error-prone technique, and the stem here needs a_1=b_1=1 assumed; exact bookkeeping with no options. Slightly above routine chain, like 2021-P1-Q15 (L3) telescoping.

questions.key_step: gcd(n,54)=2 means even and not a multiple of 3
questions.justification: One familiar move (count evens minus multiples of 6 over the four-digit range), as in the single inclusion-exclusion count 2021-P2-Q17 (L1).

questions.key_step: Common terms form an AP with difference lcm(4,5)=20 starting at 11
questions.justification: Single standard result (LCM rule) after spotting the first common term; very short. Cheaper than 2023-P2-Q9 (L2), which needs further steps.

questions.key_step: Rationalise each term so the sum telescopes to (sqrt a10 - sqrt a18)/(-d)
questions.justification: Find a and d from two conditions, rationalise, telescope: three routine stages and a familiar trick; no deeper idea. Compare 2025-P2-Q15 (L4), which telescopes a harder trig sum.

questions.key_step: Count multiples of 3, 11 and 33 in 1000-2799 and use inclusion-exclusion
questions.justification: Inclusion-exclusion as in 2021-P2-Q17 (L1) but with three separate counts over a shifted range, so more arithmetic to slip on and no options; routine overall.

questions.key_step: Split the alternating sum by parity into two cubic-polynomial sums and evaluate exactly
questions.justification: No difficult idea, but expanding cubic terms and summing two polynomial sums exactly with no options carries high precision risk (heavy computation counts under F4). Below 2023-P1-Q10 (L5), above routine L2 items.

questions.key_step: First-four sum gives d, last-four sum gives n, middle terms of 14 are T7 and T8
questions.justification: Three routine AP steps in a chain with a mild trap (the last-four-sum formula); no insight needed. Like 2026-P2-Q1 (L2), which also recovers a and d then bounds.

questions.key_step: Common terms of the APs have difference lcm(4,3,5)=60; restrict to range up to 197
questions.justification: LCM idea for common terms plus congruence solving for the first term and an endpoint cut; the endpoint check is the only trap. Same as the common-term items 2023-P2-Q9 (L2).

questions.key_step: First differences in AP so the general term is a quadratic; then standard power sums
questions.justification: One familiar method (quadratic general term, then sum formulas) with options to check against; matches the single-move Level 1 anchors such as 2024-P2-Q3 (L1) and 2021-P2-Q17 (L1).

questions.key_step: Pair terms as differences of squares to get -(1+...+2022)+2023^2, then 2023=7*17^2 with gcd condition
questions.justification: Routine chain: pairing, sum formula, factorisation and a coprimality choice; no unfamiliar idea but a few stages, like 2023-P2-Q9 (L2). The number-theory finish is lighter than 2026-P2-Q6 (L4).

questions.key_step: S_j=(j+1)/2 so the sum is a shifted sum of squares; read off A,B,C,D and test four statements
questions.justification: Several routine steps (simplify S_K, shifted power sum, expand, four option checks) but no insight; comparable to 2026-P2-Q3 (L2).

questions.key_step: Differences 3,6,9,... give a_n quadratic; then S_30 and a_40
questions.justification: Same single move as Q23: quadratic general term then power sums; arithmetic is a little longer but options allow checking. Anchor 2024-P2-Q3 (L1).
Factorisation of 33033 and a square-divisor argument, then a quadratic in r^2; routine multi-step like 2026-P2-Q12 (L2).

questions.key_step: T_n quadratic from differences 7,10,13,...; then S_29-S_9 with power sums
questions.justification: Quadratic general term plus long exact arithmetic of two cubic sums; options help but a slip is easy. Like 2026-P2-Q3 (L2).

questions.justification: Three routine stages (mean to d, form y_i, power sums) with no insight; like 2026-P2-Q12 (L2) which also recovers data from means.

questions.key_step: Weighted AM-GM by splitting a,b,c into 5,3,2 equal parts
questions.justification: One well-known trick (weighted AM-GM) applied once, with options; like 2021-P2-Q17 (L1).

questions.key_step: a_n=S_n-S_{n-1}=4/(n(n+1)(n+2)); telescope k(k+1)(k+2); read primorial 30030
questions.justification: Three linked routine moves (difference of partial sums, four-term telescoping, prime factorisation); lighter than the telescoping anchors 2021-P1-Q15 (L3) and 2025-P2-Q15 (L4), so Level 2.

questions.key_step: Sum 12 terms of the r-th AP (first term r, difference 2r-1), then sum over r
questions.justification: Direct use of the AP sum formula twice with simple algebra; one familiar move, like 2026-P1-Q3 (L1).

questions.key_step: a_3a_5=(ar^3)^2 gives ar^3=1/3; then r^4+r^2=6
questions.justification: Two small simultaneous GP equations, a quadratic in r^2 and an evaluation; routine multi-step like 2026-P2-Q3 (L2).

questions.key_step: Express all means via $a,b$ and factor
questions.justification: Single setup (means in $a,b$) then one factorisation; options allow a quick numerical check. Close to the routine-chain items such as 2021-P1-Q18 (L2).

questions.key_step: Multiply by r and subtract (AGP)
questions.justification: Standard AGP subtraction with large but benign numbers where $r-1=\frac1{20}$ simplifies it; no real insight, though no options. Comparable to 2026-P2-Q3 (L2) in routine length.

questions.key_step: Divide by xyz to get 1/x+1/y+1/z
questions.justification: One substitution gives $y$, then $xz$ and $x+z$; a few routine steps without options. Like 2026-P2-Q12 (L2).

questions.key_step: Subtract the multiples of 3 (AP with d=15)
questions.justification: One familiar move: total sum minus the sum of the terms divisible by 3, both plain AP sums. Comparable to 2021-P2-Q17 (L1, inclusion-exclusion).

questions.key_step: Centre the AGP on the middle term 2
questions.justification: Needs the AP-times-GP representation centred on $2$, then a linear equation; a student has to set it up without options, but no insight beyond that. Like 2026-P2-Q12 (L2).

questions.key_step: Multiply by 1/5 and subtract
questions.justification: Routine AGP reduction but with 109 terms and a sign/end-term bookkeeping risk in a numerical answer. Nearest is 2026-P2-Q3 (L2).

questions.key_step: Two successive multiply-subtract steps to a GP
questions.justification: Needs the difference pattern $3,4,5,6$, two rounds of subtraction and then a cubic that must be solved correctly; longer chain than the other AGP items. Near 2021-P1-Q15 (L3, telescoping) in chain length.

questions.key_step: Split into alternating squares plus sum of squares
questions.justification: Spot the pairing/splitting and use two standard sum formulas; no insight, one slip changes the answer. Like 2026-P2-Q3 (L2).

questions.key_step: Recognise brackets as GP in $-\frac{2}{3}$, multiply by $\frac12+\frac13$
questions.justification: The series structure is unusual: the student must recognise the bracket pattern and find the collapsing multiplier, then sum two GPs. Idea less practised than plain AGP, so one above routine. Comparable to 2021-P1-Q15 (L3).

questions.key_step: Common terms form an AP with d=lcm; bound by smaller last term

questions.key_step: Reverse the AP and use T20=T1+19d
questions.justification: One familiar move with a small fractional computation. Like 2024-P2-Q3 (L1) in single-idea character.

questions.key_step: Odd-placed terms form a G.P. with ratio r^2, so S_all = (1+r) S_odd
questions.justification: A single familiar move (sum of all vs odd-placed terms of a G.P.) with two geometric-sum formulas and one cancellation. Same single-trick class as 2021-P2-Q17 (inclusion-exclusion, L1).
A routine chain: set up the A.M. condition, solve the quadratic and discard r=1, then see S20-S18 as the last two terms. Close to routine-chain anchors such as 2023-P2-Q9 (L2).

questions.key_step: Logs in A.P. mean G.P.: b^2=ac and (2b/3c)^2=(a/2b)(3c/a) give b:c=3:2 then a:b=3:2
questions.justification: Two log-A.P. conditions converted to G.P. conditions, then a short elimination. A routine chain of standard results with options to check, comparable to 2023-P2-Q9 (L2).

questions.key_step: Two linear equations from S20 and S10 fix a and d, then evaluate S15 - S5
questions.justification: Direct use of the A.P. sum formula twice, solving a 2x2 linear system and one evaluation; no real decision. Similar to the single-familiar-move anchors 2021-P2-Q17 (L1).

questions.key_step: Equate r^10=(b/a)^5 with r1^(p-1)=(b/a)^((p-1)/4) and compare exponents
questions.justification: Two G.P. ratios from given terms and one exponent comparison; a short routine chain with a sign subtlety that cancels. Similar to routine-chain anchors such as 2023-P2-Q9 (L2).

questions.key_step: Factor r^4-3r^2+1=(r^2-r-1)(r^2+r-1) and use r as half their difference to telescope
questions.justification: The factorisation into two quadratics that differ by $2r$ is a less common move than plain telescoping, but it is one idea followed by routine evaluation and the options let you check. Telescoping anchors: 2021-P1-Q15 (L4, harder cot^-1 telescope), 2025-P2-Q15 (L4, numerical).

questions.key_step: Coefficients sum to zero so one root is 1; the other root's sign compares b with (a+c)/2
questions.justification: Spot that 1 is a root, convert each statement to an inequality between b and (a+c)/2, then use GM-AM and an example for 'may be'. Two statements each needing a genuine check; compare 2021-P1-Q15 (L4) for multi-statement judgement and 2026-P1-Q7 (L3).

questions.key_step: Set (a+7d)^2=(a+d)(a+43d) to get d=5a, discard d=0
questions.justification: Form the G.P. condition, simplify to a linear relation and reject d=0, then apply the A.P. sum formula. A short routine chain; compare 2026-P2-Q12 (L2, routine recovery of two unknowns).

questions.key_step: (a-1)^2=3(b+1) with b=2a-3 gives a quadratic in a; a=1 is rejected
questions.justification: Mix of A.P. and G.P. conditions reduced to one quadratic with an extraneous root to discard; a routine chain with a small trap. Comparable to 2026-P2-Q12 (L2).

questions.key_step: 1/alpha + 1/beta = q/r gives 4q=3r, so the ratio is 4/3; then (alpha-beta)^2 from sum and product
questions.justification: Sum of reciprocals into the G.P. ratio, then a standard discriminant-style evaluation; two standard chapters chained with no trap. Same level as routine-chain anchors 2023-P2-Q9 (L2).

questions.key_step: Ratio a10:a5=15:7 gives 8a=3d, then S10 gives a, d; S15-S5=5(2a+19d)
questions.justification: Same A.P. formulae as Q48 but with an extra step converting the term ratio to a linear relation, then evaluation: a routine multi-step chain with no insight. Comparable to 2026-P2-Q12 (L2).

questions.key_step: Split into GP part and A.G.P. part and use the infinite-sum formula
questions.justification: One standard formula (sum of an infinite A.G.P.) applied once, with a linear equation at the end. Same one-move level as 2021-P2-Q17 (L1) and 2024-P2-Q3 (L1).

questions.key_step: Recognise a quadratic general term and cancel the n^4 part
questions.justification: Chain of fit-quadratic, square, expand and sum with power sums, ending in a division; a slip anywhere changes the number and there are no options. Nearest anchor 2026-P2-Q12 (L2) is shorter; 2025-P2-Q15 (L4) heavier.

questions.key_step: Get S_k=k(2k+1) and the sum of S_k; the ratio reduces to 4n+5
questions.justification: Routine chain: AP sum, power-sum formulas, then a double inequality; each step is standard and nothing needs insight. Same level as 2021-P1-Q18 (L2).

questions.key_step: Complete the squares to get b^2=ac, then solve the triangle inequalities for the ratio
questions.justification: A hidden sum-of-squares step gives a GP, then three triangle inequalities and an interval; two ideas linked and an unfamiliar first move, no options for checking. Nearest 2021-P1-Q15 (L3), a little below 2026-P2-Q6 (L4).

questions.key_step: Common terms form an AP with difference lcm(4,3)=12
questions.justification: Standard common-terms routine: find first common term, lcm difference, count, sum; several routine steps with no insight, numerical so a slip is fatal. Matches the level-2 routine chain (2023-P2-Q9, L2).

questions.key_step: Triangle inequality on a/r, a, ar gives r < (1+sqrt5)/2
questions.justification: Two short linked ideas (G.P. sides with the triangle inequality, then floor function values) with a quadratic inequality; routine multi-step with no real trap. Level-2 routine chain like 2021-P1-Q18 (L2); a little above one-move items such as 2025-P1-Q7 (L1).

questions.key_step: Combine p^2=2q with q-2=6(p-2) and reject the degenerate root
questions.justification: Standard AP/GP simultaneous-equation question: a quadratic, a rejected root and a final index; routine multi-step with an option set. Same level as 2026-P2-Q12 (L2).

questions.key_step: Reduce to power sums and cancel n(n+1)/2
questions.justification: Routine chain of power-sum formulas with arithmetic at $n=100$; several standard steps, options available to verify. Level-2 routine (2021-P1-Q18, L2).

questions.key_step: Mean of AP is its middle term, then the GP condition gives a quadratic with the root fixed by a>10
questions.justification: Standard AP+GP simultaneous setup with a quadratic and a selected root; routine chain of three steps, and the distractor 312 punishes dropping the condition a>10. Level-2 routine (2026-P2-Q12 type).

questions.key_step: Rationalise and split into partial fractions: two telescoping sums
questions.justification: Two familiar telescoping tricks, each applied once, then substitution into a line; short with options. Same one-move character as 2021-P2-Q17 (L1) and 2026-P1-Q3 (L1).

questions.key_step: AP middle-term condition, then AM-GM on both reciprocal pairs
questions.justification: One familiar move (AM-GM on reciprocal pairs, equality at x=0) after the AP relation; short with options. Same one-move level as 2025-P1-Q7 (L1).

questions.key_step: Medial triangle gives ratios 1/2 (perimeter) and 1/4 (area): two infinite G.P. sums
questions.justification: One familiar idea applied twice (two infinite G.P. sums, then eliminate a); options available. Comparable to the single-move Level 1 items 2026-P1-Q3 and 2021-P2-Q17.

questions.key_step: Model daily strength as an A.P. over 25 days and equate to 17m
questions.justification: Translating the word problem into an A.P. (25 days, 4 fewer systems per day) and then a routine A.P. sum; no real insight but several chained steps. Level of 2026-P2-Q3 style routine chains.

questions.key_step: Eliminate a by squaring and dividing, giving r^2+1/r^2 = 10/3
questions.justification: Two equations in a and r, eliminated by one standard ratio trick, then a quadratic in r^2 and a short evaluation; routine chain with no insight. Similar in depth to the Level 2 routine items.

questions.key_step: Constant difference lets each term split as (1/d)(1/p - 1/q) and telescope
questions.justification: Single standard telescoping trick on an A.P. reciprocal series, followed by a one-line equation; options available. Same one-move character as the Level 1 anchors.

questions.key_step: Cube the sum and divide to cancel a, then solve a quadratic in r and reject |r|>1
questions.justification: Familiar infinite G.P. formulas, one elimination trick and a quadratic with the convergence check; routine multi-step without real insight. Matches the Level 2 routine-chain anchors.

questions.key_step: Difference of squares turns A_k into -d times a partial sum, then two simultaneous equations
questions.justification: The key idea (alternating squares become -d S_2k) is standard but needs spotting, followed by two equations, a sign check and the final evaluation with no options to verify against. Lower than 2025-P1-Q12 (L4), which has a harder functional-equation layer.

questions.key_step: Solve the recurrence in closed form, sum two G.P.s and compare the quadratic factor
questions.justification: Needs a recurrence-solving idea (not a bare formula), two G.P. sums and a final matching; each stage is standard but a slip changes the number with no options. Comparable to 2023-P1-Q10 (L4) in kind, but shorter and with a guide in the given form.

questions.key_step: Multiply by the ratio and subtract to get a G.P. sum, then substitute x = 60 and identify a, b
questions.justification: The multiply-and-subtract trick is standard, but the algebra with powers of 61 and reading off a and b must be exact, with no options. Similar in demand to routine numerical series items one level below the heavy-grind Level 4 anchors.

questions.key_step: Row n ends at the triangular number n(n+1)/2; locate 5310 between consecutive ones
questions.justification: One familiar idea (triangular numbers) and a short arithmetic check; numerical format adds slight risk but nothing branches. Very close to a single-move Level 1 problem.

questions.key_step: Fit a quadratic to the first terms of rows, then sum row 10 as an A.P.
questions.justification: Routine pattern-recognition: quadratic through three data points, then a standard A.P. sum; no deep idea, several steps, numerical format. Level 2 like other routine chains.

questions.key_step: Alternating harmonic sum = H_2n - H_n, then match two blocks of 1012 consecutive reciprocals
questions.justification: The H_2n - H_n identity is a known but not routine move, followed by careful index bookkeeping with 1/2024 absorbed into the block; slips are easy and there are no options. Below 2025-P2-Q15 (L4), which has heavier trigonometric telescoping.
